source: Scouts BSA merit badge requirements, summarized

badges.name: American Business
badges.summary: Explain how businesses are owned, financed and run; study the role of capital, profit and stock; interview a business owner; and take part in or analyze a small business project.
badges.toughestPart: Analyzing or running a real business project

badges.name: American Cultures
badges.summary: Study three different racial, ethnic or religious groups in the U.S.: their traditions, contributions and challenges. Attend a cultural event or talk with members, and discuss how to counter prejudice.
badges.toughestPart: Attending events and interviewing community members

badges.name: American Heritage
badges.summary: Discuss the Declaration of Independence and other founding ideas, research a historic person, place or event, learn the history of the flag and national symbols, and complete a heritage project.
badges.toughestPart: The research project on a historic site or family history

badges.name: American Indian Culture
badges.summary: Learn about a specific tribe: its history, government, language and life today. Explore treaties and tribal sovereignty, and complete projects such as visiting a cultural center or learning a traditional skill with tribal guidance. Replaced Indian Lore in January 2026.
badges.toughestPart: Building research on one tribe with input from tribal sources

badges.name: American Labor
badges.summary: Learn the history of organized labor, how unions and collective bargaining work, and current workplace issues like safety, wages and benefits. Interview workers or a labor representative.
badges.toughestPart: Interviewing workers and a labor leader

badges.name: Animal Science
badges.summary: Study animal health, nutrition, breeding and the economics of livestock. Pick a track (beef, dairy, horses, sheep, swine or poultry), visit a farm or ranch, and care for or study animals over time.
badges.toughestPart: Arranging a visit to a working farm or ranch

badges.name: Animation
badges.summary: Learn animation history and the principles of motion, try several techniques (flipbook, stop-motion, digital), and create your own short animated piece. Explore animation careers.

badges.name: Archaeology
badges.summary: Learn how archaeologists find, excavate, date and interpret sites. Study artifact laws and ethics, take part in a dig or lab session (or a simulated one), and research a site. Career requirement added in 2026.
badges.toughestPart: Getting a supervised dig or lab experience

badges.name: Archery
badges.summary: Learn range safety, equipment and arrow care, then shoot qualifying scores at set distances in target, field or compound archery under a certified instructor.

badges.name: Architecture
badges.summary: Tour a building and analyze its design, meet with an architect, learn drafting basics, and design a floor plan or site plan for a real or imagined space. Explore careers in architecture.
badges.toughestPart: Drafting a complete floor plan to scale

badges.name: Art
badges.summary: Learn the elements and principles of design, work in several media, create original artwork, and visit a museum, gallery or artist's studio. Explore art careers.
badges.toughestPart: Producing multiple finished pieces in different media

badges.name: Artificial Intelligence
badges.summary: Learn what AI and automation are, where each is used, and the ethics of AI including deepfakes. Practice writing clear prompts, then plan an AI project or teach a short lesson, and explore AI careers.
badges.toughestPart: The practical project or lesson you design and teach

badges.name: Astronomy
badges.summary: Identify constellations and planets, learn telescope and binocular use, observe and sketch the Moon and planets across several nights, and visit a planetarium or observatory. Explore careers.
badges.toughestPart: Repeated night observations that depend on clear weather

badges.name: Athletics
badges.summary: Learn safety and conditioning, choose events across sprints, distance, jumps and throws, set baselines, follow a training plan, and retest to show improvement. 2026 update drops the physical exam and adds careers.

badges.name: Automotive Maintenance
badges.summary: Read an owner's manual, learn the major vehicle systems, check fluids, tires, belts and lights, change a tire, figure the cost of owning a car, and perform basic maintenance with an adult.
badges.toughestPart: Hands-on maintenance tasks on a real vehicle

badges.name: Aviation
badges.summary: Learn aircraft parts, forces of flight, instruments and airspace. Build and fly a model aircraft or use a flight simulator, and visit an airport, tower or take an orientation flight.
badges.toughestPart: Arranging an airport visit or orientation flight

badges.name: Backpacking
badges.summary: Learn gear, menus, water treatment, navigation and Leave No Trace. Take three backpacking trips of at least 2 nights and 15 miles each, then plan and lead a trek of at least 5 days and 30 miles.

badges.name: Basketry
badges.summary: Learn basket materials and weaving methods, then make several baskets including square, round and seat-weaving projects.

badges.name: Bird Study
badges.summary: Learn bird anatomy, behavior and identification. Use binoculars and field guides to observe and identify at least 20 species in the wild, keep field notes, and build a feeder or nest box.

badges.name: Bugling
badges.summary: Learn the bugle's history and care, then sound the standard Scout camp calls accurately and serve as your troop's bugler for three months.
badges.toughestPart: Learning the instrument and three months of service
badges.note: Serve as troop bugler for three months

badges.name: Camping
badges.summary: Learn camp safety, gear, menus and Leave No Trace; plan campouts; and log 20 days and nights of camping, including one long-term camp, plus activities such as a hike, climb or service project while camping.

badges.name: Canoeing
badges.summary: Pass the BSA swimmer test, learn canoe parts, strokes and Safety Afloat, and demonstrate solo and tandem paddling, rescues and capsize recovery. Plan a canoe trip.
badges.toughestPart: Solo paddling control and capsize recovery

badges.name: Chemistry
badges.summary: Explore reactions, mixtures and the periodic table through hands-on experiments. Study chemistry in everyday products and the environment, and visit a lab or interview a chemist.
badges.toughestPart: Running and explaining a set of experiments

badges.name: Chess
badges.summary: Learn chess history, notation and how each piece moves; study openings, tactics and endgames; solve puzzles; and play in or organize a small tournament.
badges.toughestPart: Running or playing in a tournament

badges.name: Citizenship in Society
badges.summary: Explore what leadership and ethical decision-making mean, discuss how to make others feel welcome and included, connect with a Scout whose background differs from yours, interview someone who has made their community more welcoming, and study an event that changed how society viewed a group of people. Discontinued February 27, 2026: Scouts who already started may finish by December 31, 2026.
badges.toughestPart: Finishing all eleven discussion requirements by December 31, 2026

badges.name: Citizenship in the Community
badges.summary: Learn how your local government works, attend a public meeting, research a community issue, interview a civic leader, and complete 8 hours of volunteer service with a community organization.
badges.toughestPart: Attending a public meeting and 8 service hours

badges.name: Citizenship in the Nation
badges.summary: Study the founding documents and the three branches of government, visit a historic site or government facility, watch Congress in session, write to a member of Congress, and discuss citizen rights and duties.
badges.toughestPart: Writing to Congress and the site visit

badges.name: Citizenship in the World
badges.summary: Learn about international relations, world organizations and human rights. Study another country's government and economy, and attend a world event or talk with people from other countries.
badges.toughestPart: Comparing another nation's system in depth

badges.name: Climbing
badges.summary: Learn climbing safety, gear, knots, belaying and rappelling. Climb several routes and rappel under qualified supervision at an approved site or climbing gym.

badges.name: Coin Collecting
badges.summary: Learn how coins are minted and graded, identify mint marks and design features, build a coin set, and visit a coin show, club or museum.

badges.name: Collections
badges.summary: Build and organize a collection of your choice, catalog and preserve it properly, and share what you've learned with others.

badges.name: Communication
badges.summary: Practice listening and speaking: keep a communication log, give speeches and introductions, teach a skill, plan and run a troop event, write a letter to the editor, and study how media shape messages.
badges.toughestPart: Planning and leading a troop program

badges.name: Competitive Gaming
badges.summary: Trace the history of video gaming and esports, practice good sportsmanship and online safety, and track your gaming, activity and sleep for two weeks before building a balanced schedule. Compare gaming platforms, serve others, and explore esports careers.
badges.toughestPart: Tracking gaming, activity and sleep for two weeks, then following a balanced week

badges.name: Composite Materials
badges.summary: Learn what composites are and how they are used, compare their properties to other materials, and make a composite part safely.

badges.name: Cooking
badges.summary: Learn food safety, nutrition and menu planning. Plan, cook and serve meals at home, in camp for your patrol, and on the trail using different cooking methods.
badges.toughestPart: Planning and cooking many meals in three settings

badges.name: Crime Prevention
badges.summary: Learn how crime affects communities, do a home security check, discuss drugs, gangs and cybercrime, and plan a crime prevention program for your community.

badges.name: Cybersecurity
badges.summary: Learn digital safety and ethics, common cyber threats, and how to defend computers and networks. Complete hands-on security tasks such as strong passwords and updates, try a cryptography activity, and explore careers.
badges.toughestPart: The hands-on system security and cryptography tasks

badges.name: Cycling
badges.summary: Learn bike safety, maintenance and repair, then complete a series of progressive rides: two each of 10, 15 and 25 miles and a 50-mile ride in 8 hours (or a mountain-bike option).
badges.note: Two each of 10, 15 and 25 miles, plus a 50-mile ride

badges.name: Dentistry
badges.summary: Learn tooth anatomy and oral health, visit a dental office, explore dental careers, and make a model or demonstrate proper brushing and flossing.

badges.name: Digital Technology
badges.summary: Learn how digital devices store and transmit information, practice online safety and digital citizenship, and use technology to create something. Updated for 2026 with QR codes and current online-safety topics.

badges.name: Disabilities Awareness
badges.summary: Learn about types of disabilities and accessibility laws, visit an agency or program, do an accessibility survey, and spend time with or serve people who have disabilities.
badges.toughestPart: Sustained involvement with a disability program

badges.name: Dog Care
badges.summary: Learn breeds, care, nutrition, training and health; care for a dog for two months while keeping a log; and learn canine first aid and responsible ownership.
badges.toughestPart: Two months of daily care log
badges.note: Care for a dog for two months

badges.name: Drafting
badges.summary: Learn drafting tools and conventions, create both hand-drawn and CAD drawings, and produce a plan or technical drawing.
badges.toughestPart: Producing accurate drawings in two methods

badges.name: Electricity
badges.summary: Learn circuits, electrical safety and basic laws; build simple circuits and an electromagnet; read a meter; and do a home electrical safety check.

badges.name: Electronics
badges.summary: Learn components and schematics, solder safely, and build analog and digital circuits; troubleshoot a project.

badges.name: Emergency Preparedness
badges.summary: Learn the phases of emergency management, prepare a family plan and kit, learn how to respond to different disasters, and take part in a mock drill or emergency service project.
badges.toughestPart: Participating in a mock drill or service project

badges.name: Energy
badges.summary: Learn energy forms and sources, do a home energy audit, study efficiency, and explore future energy technologies.

badges.name: Engineering
badges.summary: Learn the engineering design process, examine how a machine works, interview an engineer, and design a solution to a real problem.
badges.toughestPart: Designing a solution end to end

badges.name: Entrepreneurship
badges.summary: Identify a business opportunity, write a business plan, and launch and run the venture, then report on results.
badges.toughestPart: Actually launching and running a business

badges.name: Environmental Science
badges.summary: Study ecology concepts, complete activities across several areas (air, water, land, endangered species, pollution prevention), and conduct a field study observing an ecosystem over time.

badges.name: Exploration
badges.summary: Learn the history of exploration, plan an expedition, practice field skills and equipment use, and carry out an exploration expedition with documented findings.

badges.name: Family Life
badges.summary: Discuss family roles and values, complete a 90-day home chore plan, carry out individual and family projects, and plan and hold family meetings on several topics.

badges.name: Farm Mechanics
badges.summary: Learn farm machinery and safety, perform maintenance on equipment, and complete a mechanical repair or project.

badges.name: Fingerprinting
badges.summary: Learn the history of fingerprinting and how prints are classified, identify the basic pattern types (arches, loops, whorls), and take a complete, readable set of your own prints.

badges.name: Fire Safety
badges.summary: Learn how fires start and spread, inspect your home for hazards, create an escape plan and run a drill, learn extinguisher use, and visit a fire station.

badges.name: First Aid
badges.summary: Learn to prevent and treat injuries and illnesses including bleeding, shock, burns, fractures, hypothermia and heat illness; demonstrate CPR and AED use and victim transport.

badges.name: Fish and Wildlife Management
badges.summary: Learn wildlife habitats and management practices, study invasive species and laws, and complete a habitat improvement project or species survey.

badges.name: Fishing
badges.summary: Learn tackle, knots and fishing regulations, cast accurately with spinning or baitcasting gear, and catch, identify, clean and cook a fish.

badges.name: Fly Fishing
badges.summary: Learn fly tackle and casting, tie flies and knots, demonstrate casting, and catch and release a fish on a fly.
badges.toughestPart: Catching a fish on a fly

badges.name: Forestry
badges.summary: Identify trees, learn forest ecology and management, measure trees, and visit a managed forest or complete a forestry project.

badges.name: Game Design
badges.summary: Learn game types and design elements, analyze existing games, design and playtest an original game, and present it.

badges.name: Gardening
badges.summary: Plan a garden, prepare soil, grow vegetables or flowers through a season, keep a log, compost, and harvest and use what you grow.

badges.name: Genealogy
badges.summary: Research your family tree, interview relatives, gather vital records, and create pedigree charts and family group sheets.

badges.name: Geocaching
badges.summary: Learn GPS use and geocaching rules, find several caches, hide or place a cache or trackable, and plan a geocaching event.

badges.name: Geology
badges.summary: Learn rock types and geologic processes, collect and identify rocks and minerals, and visit a geologic site, lab or museum.

badges.name: Golf
badges.summary: Learn the rules, etiquette and history of golf, practice grip, stance and the full swing, chip and putt, and play rounds while keeping score and following course safety.

badges.name: Graphic Arts
badges.summary: Learn the major printing processes, design a printed piece, and produce it using offset, screen, digital or another method.

badges.name: Health Care Professions
badges.summary: Explore careers across health care fields, visit a care facility, and interview health care professionals.
badges.toughestPart: Arranging interviews and the facility visit

badges.name: Hiking
badges.summary: Learn hiking safety and first aid, then take five 10-mile hikes and one 20-mile hike, each completed in a day and followed by a written report.

badges.name: Home Repairs
badges.summary: Complete a set of household repairs such as fixing a faucet, patching drywall, clearing drains, and caulking, and learn home safety.

badges.name: Horsemanship
badges.summary: Learn horse care, tack and safety, and ride while demonstrating gaits and control under supervision.
badges.toughestPart: Access to horses and riding instruction

badges.name: Insect Study
badges.summary: Learn insect anatomy and life cycles, collect and identify insects, and observe a colony or raise insects through metamorphosis.
badges.toughestPart: Raising insects through a life cycle

badges.name: Inventing
badges.summary: Learn the history of inventions and patents, then invent, build and present a working prototype.

badges.name: Journalism
badges.summary: Learn news writing, ethics and media types; write articles or produce a broadcast; and visit a newsroom.

badges.name: Kayaking
badges.summary: Pass the BSA swimmer test, learn kayak types, gear and Safety Afloat, demonstrate forward, reverse and turning strokes, a wet exit, and assisted rescues, and paddle a short course.

badges.name: Landscape Architecture
badges.summary: Visit a landscape project, study design principles, and create a landscape plan for a site.

badges.name: Law
badges.summary: Learn how laws are made and enforced, the history of law and the court system, and different kinds of law. Observe a trial or hearing, interview a lawyer or judge, and explore legal careers.

badges.name: Leatherwork
badges.summary: Learn leather types and tools, then tool, stamp and finish several leather projects.

badges.name: Lifesaving
badges.summary: Pass demanding swim tests including a 400-yard swim, then demonstrate reaching, throwing and swimming rescues, defensive escapes and in-water skills.
badges.toughestPart: Swimming rescues with a struggling victim

badges.name: Mammal Study
badges.summary: Learn how mammals are classified and adapted to their habitats, observe and record wild mammals or their signs, and complete a project such as tracking, a habitat survey or a museum visit.

badges.name: Metalwork
badges.summary: Learn metalworking safety and tools, and complete projects in sheet metal, casting, silversmithing or blacksmithing.
badges.toughestPart: Access to a supervised metal shop

badges.name: Mining in Society
badges.summary: Learn mining history, how minerals are used in everyday life, and mining's environmental impact; visit a mine or museum.
badges.toughestPart: Arranging a mine or museum visit

badges.name: Model Design and Building
badges.summary: Plan, design and build a scale model of a structure, vehicle or device.

badges.name: Motorboating
badges.summary: Pass the BSA swimmer test, learn boat handling and Safety Afloat, and operate a motorboat. 2026 update removes the CPR requirement.
badges.toughestPart: Access to a boat and qualified supervision

badges.name: Moviemaking
badges.summary: Learn storyboarding, camera work and editing, and produce a short film. 2026 update adds a career requirement.

badges.name: Multisport
badges.summary: Learn safety, gear and transitions for triathlon-style events, follow a structured training plan, and compete in two multisport races such as a triathlon, duathlon or aquathlon.
badges.toughestPart: Training for and finishing two races

badges.name: Music
badges.summary: Learn music theory, notation and the history of several genres, perform pieces on an instrument or by voice, attend live performances, and explore careers in music.

badges.name: Nature
badges.summary: Learn how ecosystems work and the food web, then study and identify species across several groups (birds, mammals, reptiles, insects, fish, plants, rocks) in the field.

badges.name: Nuclear Science
badges.summary: Learn atomic structure, radiation types and safety, build an atom model, use a detector or cloud chamber, and explore nuclear energy, medicine and careers.

badges.name: Oceanography
badges.summary: Learn ocean currents, waves, tides and marine life, run experiments on salinity or density, and complete a project such as a model, report or visit to a marine facility.

badges.name: Orienteering
badges.summary: Learn map symbols, compass use and pace counting, complete several orienteering courses including a competitive event, and design and set up a course of your own.

badges.name: Painting
badges.summary: Learn paint types, surface preparation and safety, and complete interior and exterior painting jobs plus a decorative project. Explore careers in the painting trade.

badges.name: Personal Fitness
badges.summary: Get a health exam, take a fitness test, then follow a 12-week personal exercise program, logging progress and retesting at the end.

badges.name: Personal Management
badges.summary: Learn budgeting, saving and investing; track income and expenses for 13 weeks; set goals; plan a major purchase; and manage your time with a one-week to-do plan.
badges.note: Track income and expenses for 13 weeks

badges.name: Pets
badges.summary: Choose a pet and care for it for two months while keeping a log of feeding, grooming and behavior; learn its needs, health issues and training.
badges.note: Care for a pet for two months

badges.name: Photography
badges.summary: Learn camera controls, exposure and composition, shoot a photo story or essay, edit and share your images, and explore careers in photography.

badges.name: Pioneering
badges.summary: Tie and use knots, whippings and lashings, learn rope care and safety, and build pioneering structures such as a monkey bridge, tower or trestle with your patrol.

badges.name: Plant Science
badges.summary: Study plant structure, growth and agriculture, then choose a track (agronomy, horticulture or field botany) to grow plants or run an experiment over a growing season.

badges.name: Plumbing
badges.summary: Learn how water supply and drain systems work, repair a faucet, clear a clogged drain, cut and join copper or plastic pipe, and practice plumbing safety.

badges.name: Pottery
badges.summary: Learn clay types and techniques, make pots by hand-building and on the wheel, decorate and glaze them, and see how pieces are fired in a kiln.
badges.toughestPart: Access to a kiln and wheel

badges.name: Programming
badges.summary: Learn programming history, languages and how code is executed; write and run programs in several languages; and discuss intellectual property and programming careers.
badges.toughestPart: Writing working code in multiple languages

badges.name: Public Health
badges.summary: Learn how diseases spread, the roles of public health agencies, vaccines and sanitation, and visit a public health department or facility.

badges.name: Public Speaking
badges.summary: Prepare and give several speeches including an informative talk, a persuasive talk and an impromptu speech, and learn to introduce a speaker.

badges.name: Pulp and Paper
badges.summary: Learn the history of papermaking and how pulp is produced and recycled, make a sheet of paper by hand, and visit a mill or explore the industry.

badges.name: Radio
badges.summary: Learn how radio waves travel and how stations work, then choose amateur, broadcast or shortwave radio and operate or monitor under supervision. Updated in 2026 for modern devices.

badges.name: Railroading
badges.summary: Learn railroad history, types of equipment and rail safety, ride a train or visit a rail facility, and build or operate a model railroad layout.

badges.name: Reading
badges.summary: Read books across several genres, keep notes, discuss them with others, and complete reading-related service such as reading to younger children.

badges.name: Reptile and Amphibian Study
badges.summary: Learn how reptiles and amphibians differ, identify local species, observe them in the wild, and care for one in captivity for at least a month.
badges.note: Care for a reptile or amphibian for one month

badges.name: Rifle Shooting
badges.summary: Learn firearm safety and the rules of the range, practice positions and marksmanship, and shoot a qualifying score with a .22 rifle or air rifle under a certified instructor.

badges.name: Robotics
badges.summary: Learn robot types, sensors and programming; design, build and program a robot to complete a task; and present your work and explore robotics careers.
badges.toughestPart: Building and programming a working robot

badges.name: Rowing
badges.summary: Pass the BSA swimmer test, learn boat parts, rowing strokes and Safety Afloat, demonstrate maneuvers and capsize recovery, and complete a long-distance row.

badges.name: Safety
badges.summary: Learn about safety at home, school, online and in the community; conduct safety inspections; and plan a safety event. 2026 update adds online-safety topics.

badges.name: Salesmanship
badges.summary: Learn the steps of a sale and customer service, research a product, and sell products or services to customers.

badges.name: Scholarship
badges.summary: Show a strong or improving school record, discuss study habits and goals, and interview teachers or school administrators about the value of education.

badges.name: Scouting Heritage
badges.summary: Learn how Scouting began and grew, research your council's history, visit a Scouting museum or historic site, and interview a long-time Scouter.

badges.name: Scuba Diving
badges.summary: Learn diving physics, physiology and safety, then complete pool training and open-water dives to earn an open-water scuba certification under a certified instructor.

badges.name: Sculpture
badges.summary: Learn sculpture tools and methods, and create sculptures in clay, plaster or wood, including a modeled piece and a carved piece.

badges.name: Search and Rescue
badges.summary: Learn how search and rescue teams are organized, search techniques and survival skills, and take part in a mock search operation.

badges.name: Shotgun Shooting
badges.summary: Learn shotgun safety, parts and ammunition, practice stance and swing, and break a qualifying number of clay targets under a certified instructor.

badges.name: Signs, Signals, and Codes
badges.summary: Learn and use Morse code, American Sign Language, trail signs, semaphore and other codes to send and receive messages.

badges.name: Skating
badges.summary: Choose ice, roller or inline skating; learn safety and equipment care; and demonstrate forward and backward skating, stops and turns.

badges.name: Small-Boat Sailing
badges.summary: Pass the BSA swimmer test, learn sailing theory, parts and points of sail, rig a boat, sail a triangular course, and perform capsize recovery.

badges.name: Snow Sports
badges.summary: Learn safety, gear and the responsibility code, then choose downhill, cross-country or snowboarding and demonstrate skills on the snow.

badges.name: Soil and Water Conservation
badges.summary: Learn how soil forms and erodes and how water cycles through watersheds, and complete a conservation project such as erosion control.

badges.name: Space Exploration
badges.summary: Learn the history and purpose of space exploration, build and launch a model rocket, and design a crewed or robotic mission.

badges.name: Sports
badges.summary: Learn sportsmanship and safety, participate in two sports for a full season, and explain the rules and strategy of each.
badges.toughestPart: A full season of two sports

badges.name: Stamp Collecting
badges.summary: Learn stamp terms and printing, use catalogs and albums, and build an organized stamp collection.

badges.name: Surveying
badges.summary: Learn surveying tools and methods, measure and map a plot of land, and explore careers in surveying and mapping.

badges.name: Sustainability
badges.summary: Track your family's water, food, energy and waste use, hold a family meeting to set goals, and complete projects across several sustainability areas.

badges.name: Swimming
badges.summary: Pass the BSA swimmer test, learn water safety, swim 150 yards using several strokes in good form, float, and perform surface dives and a safe entry.

badges.name: Textile
badges.summary: Learn about natural and synthetic fibers and how fabric is made, and complete textile projects such as weaving, knitting or sewing.

badges.name: Theater
badges.summary: Learn theater terms and roles, act in a performance, and work on a technical area such as set design, lighting or costumes.

badges.name: Traffic Safety
badges.summary: Learn how to stay safe as a pedestrian, cyclist and future driver, discuss distracted driving and seat belts, and plan a safety program. Updated for 2026.

badges.name: Truck Transportation
badges.summary: Learn how trucking moves goods, the regulations and safety rules for trucks, and visit a truck terminal or interview a driver.

badges.name: Veterinary Medicine
badges.summary: Learn about veterinary careers and specialties, the role of vets in animal and public health, and visit a veterinary clinic.

badges.name: Water Sports
badges.summary: Pass the BSA swimmer test, learn waterskiing or wakeboarding safety, and demonstrate getting up and riding behind a boat.

badges.name: Weather
badges.summary: Learn how weather forms and is forecast, make simple instruments, keep a weather log, and learn about severe weather safety.

badges.name: Welding
badges.summary: Learn welding processes, metal properties and shop safety, and make several welds under qualified supervision.

badges.name: Whitewater
badges.summary: Requires Canoeing or Kayaking first. Learn river hazards and reading water, rescue techniques, and paddle Class II whitewater with a qualified leader.

badges.name: Wilderness Survival
badges.summary: Learn the priorities of survival, build a survival kit and a shelter, and spend a night in the shelter you build.
badges.toughestPart: A night in your own shelter

badges.name: Wildland Fire Management
badges.summary: Learn the history, causes and effects of wildfire, how prescribed fire is used, and how fire behaves. Study firefighter safety, suppression tactics and the Incident Command System, demonstrate hand tools, and complete a prevention or readiness project.
badges.toughestPart: Demonstrating fireline tools and the Taking Action project

badges.name: Woodcarving
badges.summary: Learn carving tools, sharpening and knife safety, and carve several projects in relief and in the round.

badges.name: Woodwork
badges.summary: Learn wood types, tools and joinery, and build finished woodwork projects.
